segments.text: In the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, the Circumcircle is the unique circle passing through the three vertices A, B, and C of reference triangle A B C. Its center is the Circumcenter X three, the concurrence of the three perpendicular bisectors of the sides.

segments.text: By the Law of Sines, the diameter two R of the circumcircle equals a over sine A, b over sine B, and c over sine C, giving circumradius R equal to a b c divided by four Delta. Its homogeneous barycentric equation is a squared v w plus b squared w u plus c squared u v equals zero.

segments.text: In Collection One, the circumcircle is theisogonal dual of the line at infinity, the circle of inversion exchanging the Isodynamic Points X fifteen and X sixteen, and the parent of the Nine-Point Circle under one-half dilation.
